doc.title: Dianne Reeves interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, October 13, 2001

title: Working with Sergio Mendes and Brazilian music
summary: Mendes exposed her to Brazilian writers and singers such as Elis Regina, Ivan Lins and Milton Nascimento.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Great answer. You work with Sergio Mendes also?
Same kind of experience with him?

Yeah, that was pretty amazing because while we performed the music of “Brazil ’66,” I have to say both Harry and Sergio really were into exposing you to writers that you wouldn’t normally hear about. And when I was working with Sergio he would give me tapes and live performances of people that I had no idea who they were, people like Elis Regina or Maria Bethania or Caetano Veloso or all or these great writers and singers from Brazil. Ivan Lins, the first time I heard him was some songs that he had written that he sent to Sergio, he’s like check this guy out. Beautiful songs. And of course I knew a little bit about Milton Nascimento but not as much as I did after working with Sergio. So there was a lot of behind the scenes things.
